item.text: Both approved posts are accepted and the campaign is live, targeting UK adults aged 18+. It has a $450 lifetime cap, roughly $32.14 daily pacing, and an automatic end at midnight UK time after December 31. I’ll check delivery and costs regularly over the two weeks.
The first day spent $31.97 for 19,428 impressions and 8 link clicks—about $4 per click. Both posts have similar click costs so far; I’ll collect another day before changing bids.
After three days, spend is $92.47 with 35 link clicks. Click costs have improved, and I’m testing a $2 maximum bid to seek more clicks within the budget while watching for reduced delivery.
The bid limits reduced delivery too much: the last two days added only 9 clicks. I’ve restored automatic bidding and adjusted daily pacing for the remaining days, keeping the $450 lifetime cap.

At the halfway point, the campaign has spent $177.34 for 161,485 impressions and 66 link clicks. The “£0. Thirty seconds” post has a lower average click cost so far ($2.29 versus $3.06); both remain active as delivery continues.

item.text: With four days left, spend is $285.68 and the campaign has delivered 118 link clicks. Recent clicks average about $2.08. I’ve adjusted daily pacing to approximately $41 to use the remaining budget through New Year’s Eve.
The final day begins with $405.18 spent and 172 link clicks. The remaining $44.82 is available for today, and the campaign is scheduled to stop at midnight.

The campaign ran December 18–31, UK time, and is now stopped. I monitored it daily and adjusted bidding and pacing.

- **Spend:** $449.71 of $450
- **Impressions:** 446,193
